rounds.text: Hester Biosciences Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive EV/EBITDA of 10.72x against a sector benchmark of 17.71x [E11]. This undervaluation contrasts sharply with strong profitability metrics, including an impressive Return on Assets (ROA) of 20.2% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 6.34% [E8]. Operational efficiency is further highlighted by a sharp reduction in working capital requirements from 80.2 days down to 54.4 days [E61], alongside robust cash generation where operating cash flow reached Rs 64 Cr and covered 90% of operating profit in Mar 2026 [E35, E37]. Moreover, capital expenditure appears largely completed as evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) dropping by 95.1% to Rs 9 Cr, pointing toward newly unlocked operational capacity [E41]. Earnings momentum is accelerating, demonstrated by a 41% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 [E21, E67]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 9.19% over the past five years [E63] and earnings include a notable other income component of Rs. 105 Cr [E66].

Hester Biosciences carries significant fundamental and valuation risks that challenge its recent price appreciation. The core business growth exhibits severe sluggishness, evidenced by compounded sales growth over the past five years at a modest 9% [E15], dropping further to just 4% over the trailing twelve months [E17], alongside a flagged poor sales growth performance [E63] and screen alerts noting a year-over-year sales contraction [E72]. Valuation metrics are heavily stretched, with the stock trading at a lofty P/E of 35.8 [E1] and an expensive price-to-book ratio of 5.30x [E2], which is notably higher than the sector benchmark P/B of 3.15x [E7]. Furthermore, reported earnings quality is compromised by non-operating factors, specifically a flagged massive other income component of Rs. 105 Cr [E66] and a warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E65]. Institutional confidence is conspicuously lacking, demonstrated by negative institutional money flows [E45], an institutional outflow screen flag [E74], and virtually non-existent domestic institutional holdings at 0.00% alongside declining foreign institutional participation [E43, E44]. Finally, the equity carries extreme historical volatility of 44.3% [E55] and a severe worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -60.9% [E54]. Conceded: the company displays strong short-term profitability metrics, including a 41% TTM profit growth [E21], expanding operating margins [E31, E71], and solid operating cash flow backed by completed capital expenditures [E34, E41].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is a modest 9% [E15] and TTM sales growth sits at 4% [E17]. However, the bear's focus on sluggish top-line metrics ignores a massive acceleration in bottom-line profitability, with 3-year profit growth at 26% and TTM profit growth surging by 41% [E20, E21], fueled by operating margins expanding to 27% [E30]. Conceded: other income includes Rs. 105 Cr [E66] and the stock trades at a P/E of 35.8 [E1]. Yet, this valuation is offset by an EV/EBITDA of just 10.72x—which sits well below the sector benchmark of 17.71x [E11]—and a reverse DCF showing today's price implies a mere 3.2% earnings growth against the 8.0% base case [E48]. Conceded: the bear highlights negative institutional money flows and low institutional holdings [E43, E44, E45]. Nevertheless, these concerns are neutralized by outstanding operational efficiency, as evidenced by capital expenditures winding down with CWIP dropping 95.1% to Rs. 9 Cr [E41], working capital requirements improving from 80.2 to 54.4 days [E61], and robust free cash flow reaching Rs. 47 Cr [E36].

Conceded: operating margins have expanded to 27% [E30] and CWIP dropped by 95.1% to Rs. 9 Cr [E41]. However, pointing to an EV/EBITDA of 10.72x [E11] ignores the fact that headline valuation remains stretched at a P/E of 35.8x and a price-to-book ratio of 5.30x [E1, E2], the latter flagged explicitly as a negative because it sits well above the sector benchmark of 3.15x [E7, E62]. Conceded: working capital requirements have improved to 54.4 days [E61] and free cash flow reached Rs. 47 Cr [E36]. Nevertheless, earnings quality is severely compromised by the inclusion of Rs. 105 Cr in other income [E66] alongside explicit warnings that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E65]. Furthermore, dismissing top-line weakness by citing surging profit growth ignores the reality that trailing twelve-month sales growth has slowed to 4% [E17], 5-year sales growth is a poor 9.19% [E63], and recent quarterly margins are flagged as inconsistent [E33]. Finally, the bull's reliance on a reverse DCF implying 3.2% growth [E48] overlooks ongoing institutional outflow [E74], negative money flow [E45], and a heavy historical drawdown risk of -60.9% [E54].
